evidence_summary: Laminin-332 perturbation and alpha3beta1 blockade resolve a matrix-to-integrin focal-adhesion relay with FAK/SRC readouts.
limitations: Carcinoma mechanistic anchor; gamma2-containing laminin matrix was perturbed as a complex rather than isolated LAMA3.

context_scope: integrin blockade and hemidesmosome-like adhesion assays
evidence_summary: Laminin-332 matrix adhesion and alpha6beta4-dependent hemidesmosome organization are resolved at the integrin-complex level.
limitations: Matrix organization and hemidesmosome assays are context-dependent; no SCI model.

evidence_summary: Recombinant laminin-411 shows alpha6beta1 binding, corroborated by laminin-411/421 alpha6beta1 adhesion and vascular-laminin assays.
limitations: Binding is modest and comparator-cell based; retain the complete alpha6beta1 heterodimer.

context_scope: soluble alpha8beta1-AP, affinity matrices, and blocking antibodies
evidence_summary: The TNC TNfn3/RGD domain supports resolved alpha8beta1 binding and adhesion in recombinant and cell-based assays.
limitations: Evidence is strongest for the defined TNC fragment/domain, not unrestricted full-length TNC.

evidence_summary: TNC binding and alphaVbeta6 assignment are supported by TNC-agarose/neutralization and independent epithelial TNC-alphaVbeta6 adhesion context.
limitations: No purified affinity measurement; cellular matrix context and complete alphaVbeta6 are required.

evidence_summary: ICAM1 engagement of LFA1 resolves an adhesion-to-Src/Rap1-actin/Pyk2 relay across independent primary studies.
limitations: LFA1 is the complete alphaLbeta2 heterodimer; relay is receptor-proximal and not a terminal TF.

evidence_summary: ICAM1 is recognized by the Mac1 alphaMbeta2 I-domain/heterodimer in direct binding and leukocyte-adhesion assays.
limitations: Preserve the complete Mac1 complex; avoid interpreting this as free ITGAM or ITGB2 binding.

evidence_summary: VCAM1 directly supports alpha9beta1 adhesion, with an independent alpha9-dependent VCAM1/FAK-Src-ERK chemotaxis study.
limitations: Complete alpha9beta1 is required; comparator/non-SCI context limits injury-specific inference.

evidence_summary: VCAM1-alpha9beta1 engagement is linked to FAK/Src/ERK chemotaxis, corroborated by direct alpha9beta1 adhesion evidence.
limitations: This is an adhesion relay rather than a terminal TF; retain alpha9beta1 complex context.

evidence_summary: Thy-1 engages the alphaVbeta3-syndecan-4 adhesion complex in cell-contact assays, with FAK/PKCalpha/RhoA/PI3K/Rac1 outputs.
limitations: Three-component contact complex and cell presentation are required; do not collapse to alphaVbeta3 alone.

evidence_summary: Thy-1 cell-cell contact through alphaVbeta3/SDC4 produces a resolved FAK/PI3K/Rac1/RhoA adhesion relay.
limitations: Relay is complex-dependent and not a terminal transcriptional readout.

evidence_summary: MAdCAM1 is a direct ligand for the alpha4beta7 adhesion receptor, with independent homing/adhesion and receptor-specific evidence.
limitations: Complete alpha4beta7 heterodimer and endothelial addressin presentation are required.

evidence_summary: MAdCAM1-alpha4beta7 engagement produces paxillin/Cas-L and homing-associated adhesion signaling, anchored by direct receptor evidence.
limitations: Proximal adhesion relay; no terminal TF and no SCI-specific model.

evidence_summary: NCAM1 homophilic engagement is supported by independent neurite/adhesion studies and resolves a Src/FAK neurite relay.
limitations: Homophilic NCAM1 presentation and neural context are required; not an ECM ligand.

evidence_summary: Nephronectin/NPNT binds alpha8beta1 and drives defined adhesion through the RGD/FEI matrix interface.
limitations: Matrix domain and complete alpha8beta1 context must be retained.

evidence_summary: Netrin-1 directly binds neogenin in structural/biophysical work and is independently confirmed within a resolved NEO1 guidance-cue complex.
limitations: Netrin family and co-receptor context must not be conflated; this row is specifically NTN1-NEO1.

evidence_summary: Podoplanin engages CLEC-2 through defined glycan/protein contacts and receptor clustering, supported by direct structure and signaling studies.
limitations: Glycosylation and receptor clustering are required; this is a platelet/immune adhesion context.

evidence_summary: Podoplanin-CLEC-2 engagement activates the resolved Src-Syk-LAT-PLCgamma2 hemITAM relay.
limitations: Relay depends on CLEC-2 clustering and cellular presentation; not a terminal TF.

evidence_summary: Pleiotrophin supports a resolved alphaVbeta3/PTPRZ1 adhesion branch, corroborated by independent PTN/PTPRZ1/alphaVbeta3 migration signaling.
limitations: PTN receptor branches are context-dependent; preserve the alphaVbeta3/PTPRZ1 co-receptor configuration.

evidence_summary: PTN binds and inhibits PTPRZ1 phosphatase activity in independent primary studies, resolving the ligand-to-receptor branch.
limitations: PTN/PTPRZ1 is a phosphatase-receptor context rather than a classical integrin; downstream effects are cell-state dependent.

evidence_summary: PTN/HB-GAM binds syndecan-3 and supports Src/cortactin-associated adhesion signaling in independent neural/osteoblast systems.
limitations: Proteoglycan glycosaminoglycan/core-protein presentation is required; preserve SDC3 specificity.

evidence_summary: Reelin directly engages ApoER2/LRP8 in binding, clustering, and Dab1/Src/Akt studies.
limitations: Reelin is a large extracellular glycoprotein and receptor clustering/context are required.

evidence_summary: Reelin directly engages VLDLR in receptor-binding and clustering studies with independent downstream signaling support.
limitations: Reelin receptor clustering and extracellular presentation are required; do not merge with LRP8.

evidence_summary: RGMA-NEO1 binding and receptor-proximal guidance branches are supported across multiple independent primary studies.
limitations: RGMA has parallel receptor/co-receptor branches; this row is specifically NEO1.

evidence_summary: Syndecan-2 association with PTPRJ/CD148 is supported by independent primary studies and linked to integrin/Src adhesion signaling.
limitations: Association is context-dependent and does not imply a freely soluble binary ligand.

evidence_summary: E-selectin recognizes the GLG1/ESL-1 glycan-bearing adhesion receptor in direct rolling/adhesion studies.
limitations: Glycan presentation and endothelial rolling context are required.

evidence_summary: Sema3A forms the defined neuropilin-1/plexin-A1 receptor complex with receptor-proximal guidance signaling.
limitations: Preserve the NRP1:PLXNA1 complex; semaphorin receptor composition is not interchangeable across plexins.

evidence_summary: Sema3G engages the defined NRP2:plexin-A1 complex in primary receptor/functional studies.
limitations: Complex composition is critical; related Sema3G/NRP2/Plexin-D1 evidence is not substituted for Plexin-A1.

evidence_summary: Sema7A binds and signals through the alpha1beta1 integrin in direct/functional primary studies.
limitations: Complete alpha1beta1 and glycosylated membrane presentation are required.

evidence_summary: SPP1/osteopontin engages CD44 variant isoforms in direct adhesion/signaling studies.
limitations: CD44 variant and glycosylation context matter; do not generalize to all CD44 forms.

evidence_summary: TGM2 associates with syndecan-4 and supports defined adhesion/FAK-linked signaling across independent studies.
limitations: Matrix crosslinking and SDC4 presentation are context-dependent; no purified binary affinity was required for this adhesion-complex promotion.

evidence_summary: The versican G3 domain supports a defined beta1-integrin interface and adhesion/FAK signaling, with independent rat ECM-interface evidence.
limitations: Promotion is domain/isoform-specific; do not generalize G3 evidence to all versican forms or infer a single alpha partner.

evidence_summary: EFNA1-EPHA4 binding and EphA4-proximal cytoskeletal/adhesion signaling are supported by receptor-selectivity and independent monocyte/neural studies.
limitations: Ephrin ligand presentation and receptor clustering are required; no SCI-specific validation.

evidence_summary: EFNA2 binds EPHA7 in direct receptor-selectivity work and independent neural signaling studies.
limitations: EphA7 isoform/processing and membrane presentation matter; no SCI-specific validation.
